text: Why does a long cable round off the corners of a square wave?
choices: The voltage decays exponentially along the cable
A square wave is a sum of a fundamental plus odd harmonics; the cable attenuates high frequencies more, removing the harmonics that make the corners
The cable's resistance limits the current at sharp edges
Reflections from the far end cancel the edges
explanation: In the frequency domain the answer is a subtraction: the sharp corners ARE the high harmonics, and a band-limited channel removes them. This is why the frequency-domain view explains what the time-domain view merely displays.
